module_title: Basics of Electricity: Charge, Current, and Ohm's Law
introduction: Electricity is the foundation of modern life. It is fundamentally the study of the flow of electrons (charges). At this level, we define the basic terms that make up every electrical circuit.

core_concepts.title: Electric Charge (Q)
core_concepts.description:
The fundamental property of matter that causes it to experience a force in electromagnetic fields. 
Types: Positive and Negative. Like charges repel, opposite charges attract. 
SI Unit: Coulomb (C).

core_concepts.title: Electric Current (I)
core_concepts.description:
The rate of flow of electric charge (electrons) through a conductor. 
Formula: $I = Q / t$ (Current = Charge / Time). 
SI Unit: Ampere (A). 
Measuring Instrument: 'Ammeter' - Always connected in 'Series' in a circuit.

core_concepts.title: Potential Difference / Voltage (V)
core_concepts.description:
The work done in moving a unit positive charge from one point to another. It is the 'push' that makes electrons flow. 
Formula: $V = W / Q$ (Voltage = Work / Charge). 
SI Unit: Volt (V). 
Measuring Instrument: 'Voltmeter' - Always connected in 'Parallel' across the components.

core_concepts.title: Ohm's Law
core_concepts.description:
Provided temperature remains constant, the current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference applied across its ends. 
Formula: $V = I \times R$. 
'Resistance' ($R$) is the opposition to the flow of current. Its unit is Ohm ($\Omega$).

important_entities.name: Properties of Ideal Meters
important_entities.significance: An 'Ideal Ammeter' must have 'ZERO' resistance (so it doesn't block the current it is trying to measure). An 'Ideal Voltmeter' must have 'INFINITE' resistance (so it draws zero current from the main circuit).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: 'What is the direction of electric current?' Remember, by physical convention, current flows from the 'Positive terminal to the Negative terminal' (+ to -). However, the actual electrons flow in the OPPOSITE direction (from - to +).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Very Important Rule (V = I x R)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To remember Ohm's Law: Put $V$ on top, $I$ and $R$ on the bottom. Need $V$? It's $I \times R$. Need $I$? It's $V/R$. Need $R$? It's $V/I$.

exam_strategy_tips: A direct question in SSC exams: 'How is a voltmeter connected in an electrical circuit?' Answer: In parallel.
